Of course! It really depends on what you like to watch, but here's a quick guide to the best options right now:

**For most people - Best Overall:**
**Netflix** - Still the biggest library and the most original hits. Best if you want a little bit of everything: dramas, comedy, true crime, reality, K-dramas, and kids stuff. Has a cheaper with-ads plan if you want to save money.

**Best for prestige movies & HBO shows:**
**Max (formerly HBO Max)** - Home to HBO originals like *The Last of Us, Succession, House of the Dragon*, plus Warner Bros. movies, DC, and Studio Ghibli. Best picture quality and most "critically acclaimed" pick.

**Best for families, Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar:**
**Disney+** - No-brainer if you have kids or love Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar, and National Geographic. The Disney Bundle (Disney+ + Hulu + ESPN+) is one of the best values in streaming.

**Best value for originals:**
**Apple TV+** - Smallest library, but almost everything on it is excellent (*Ted Lasso, Severance, Slow Horses, For All Mankind*) and it's cheaper than Netflix/Max with no ads.

**Best if you already have Prime:**
**Amazon Prime Video** - Included with Amazon Prime, so you might already have it. Great for movies to rent/buy, plus hits like *The Boys, Fallout, Reacher*, and Thursday Night Football.

**Best for network shows & next-day TV:**
**Hulu** - Great for catching up on ABC, FX, and Fox shows the next day, plus great originals and a huge movie library. Best with the Disney Bundle.

**Best budget / free-ish options:**
**Peacock, Paramount+, Tubi, Pluto TV** - Peacock (The Office, SNL) and Paramount+ (Star Trek, CBS Sports, Yellowstone universe) are cheaper. Tubi and Pluto TV are 100% free with ads.

**What about Live TV?**
If you want to replace cable for sports/news: **YouTube TV** is the best overall, **Sling TV** is the cheapest, **Hulu + Live TV** is great if you already like Hulu.

---

1. What do you watch most? (movies, binge dramas, reality, anime, sports, kids?)

3. What country are you in? (libraries differ a lot)

runs.u: Can you recommend a cloud provider?
runs.reply:
Absolutely — but the "best" one really depends on what you're building. Here's a quick breakdown to help you pick:

### The Big 3

**1. AWS (Amazon Web Services)**
*Best for: Most startups, enterprises, widest range of services*
Pros: Largest selection of services (200+), most regions, most mature, huge community/tutorials
Cons: Billing can be complex and surprising, learning curve is steep
Pick it if: You want maximum flexibility and don't want to hit a limit later.

**2. Microsoft Azure**
*Best for: Companies already using Microsoft / Windows / Office 365*
Pros: Excellent hybrid cloud + Active Directory integration, strong enterprise support, great for .NET, strong AI partnership with OpenAI
Cons: UI/portal can be confusing, documentation is hit-or-miss
Pick it if: You're a Microsoft shop or need enterprise compliance.

**3. Google Cloud (GCP)**
*Best for: Data, AI/ML, Kubernetes, startups*
Pros: Best-in-class for Kubernetes (GKE invented it), BigQuery, AI/Vertex AI, generally clean UI and generous networking pricing, great free tier
Cons: Fewer regions than AWS, smaller market share = fewer StackOverflow answers
Pick it if: You're doing AI/ML, data analytics, or cloud-native apps. Full disclosure: I run on Google Cloud!

### Best for Simple & Cheap

**4. DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Linode (Akamai), Vultr**
*Best for: Side projects, SMBs, simple VPS hosting, predictable pricing*
Pros: Super simple, flat pricing starting ~$4-6/mo, great docs, no surprise bills
Cons: Far fewer managed services (no equivalent to BigQuery, SageMaker, etc.)
Pick it if: You just need a VM, simple database, and storage without the Big Cloud complexity.

**5. Oracle Cloud, IBM Cloud**
*Best for: Specific enterprise workloads, Oracle databases, often very cheap free tier*
Oracle in particular has a very generous Always Free tier. Worth a look for hobby projects.

**6. Specialist clouds**
* AI/GPU: CoreWeave, Lambda Labs, Together AI — much cheaper and more available GPUs than the Big 3
* Edge / CDN / Serverless: Cloudflare (Workers, R2, Pages) — incredibly fast and cheap for web apps
* Private / EU-focused: OVHcloud, Scaleway — good for data sovereignty in Europe

### How to choose in 30 seconds:

* **Just learning / side project?** -> DigitalOcean, Hetzner, or GCP Free Tier + Cloudflare
* **Startup that needs to scale fast?** -> AWS or GCP
* **Enterprise / Microsoft Teams / .NET / Windows?** -> Azure
* **Data-heavy / AI / Kubernetes?** -> GCP, then Azure
* **Worried about cost?** -> Hetzner / DigitalOcean for VMs, Cloudflare R2 for storage (zero egress fees)

My general advice: Start with containers (Docker) or Kubernetes if you can. It makes it much easier to switch providers later and avoid lock-in.

First, a quick explainer:

**Network vs. Issuer:** Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover are the networks that process payments. Chase, Capital One, Citi, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, etc. are the issuers — the banks that actually give you the card, set the APR, fees, and rewards. You'll pick an issuer.

4. **Rewards style:** Do you want simple cash-back, or are you okay with tracking points/miles categories?

The golden rule for any card: If you can, pay the full statement balance every month to avoid paying interest. Rewards are never worth carrying debt.

### 2. Popular U.S. issuers by goal

**For simple cash-back / no annual fee:**
* **Discover it Cash Back** - Great starter card. No annual fee, 5% rotating categories, and Discover matches all cash back you earn the first year. Very beginner-friendly.
* **Capital One Quicksilver** - Flat 1.5% back on everything, no annual fee, no foreign transaction fees. Easy to understand.
* **Citi Double Cash or Citi Custom Cash** - Double Cash is a flat ~2% (1% when you buy + 1% when you pay). Custom Cash is great if you spend a lot in one category like groceries or dining.
* **Chase Freedom Unlimited** - Flat cash-back plus extra on travel/dining booked through Chase.

**For travel rewards:**
* **Chase Sapphire Preferred** - Very popular starter travel card. Chase Ultimate Rewards points transfer to airlines/hotels. Has an annual fee (~$95), but good value if you travel 1-2x a year.
* **Capital One Venture / Venture X** - Flat miles on everything, easy to redeem, no foreign transaction fees.
* **American Express Gold or Platinum** - Excellent Membership Rewards points for dining/travel, great perks, but higher annual fees ($250+). Best if you already spend a lot in those areas.

**For building or rebuilding credit:**
* **Discover it Secured, Capital One Platinum Secured, or cards from a local credit union** - You put down a small deposit ($200-$500) that becomes your limit. Use it lightly and pay in full for 6-12 months to build history.
* **Student cards:** Discover it Student Cash Back or Capital One Savor Student are good if you're in college.

**For low interest / balance transfers:**
* Look at credit unions or **Citi, Wells Fargo, Bank of America** - they often have 0% intro APR for 12-21 months offers. Great only if you have a plan to pay it off during the intro period.

### 3. My general take

There isn't one "best company" — these are all large, reputable issuers:

* Pick **Discover or Capital One** if you want simple, forgiving, beginner-friendly.
* Pick **Chase** if you want to get into travel points long-term.
* Pick **Amex** if you spend heavily on dining/travel and want premium perks and can justify an annual fee.
